transcript.text: Bosch HBS534BS0B oven displaying E011 and won't let me do anything. Beeping. Help!

E011 on Bosch ovens usually means either a control key is being held down continuously (a 'stuck' button) or the oven cannot read its internal temperature sensor. Since it's beeping and locking you out, let's rule out the simple cause first. Please press every single button on the panel firmly and release it to ensure none are jammed in a depressed position. If all buttons move freely and the error persists after switching the oven off at the wall for 10 minutes and turning it back on, we will then look at the temperature sensor.

Pressed every button, none feel stuck. Still E011 and beeping. Worth saying it started after I wiped the panel with a damp cloth and spray, and there's still a bit of moisture along the bottom edge. Will dry it and switch it off at the cooker switch for a few mins.

That sounds like the right approach. Moisture under the fascia can cause exactly this kind of short circuit and beeping lockout. Please ensure the oven is switched off at the wall (cooker switch) for about 10–15 minutes to allow any residual charge in the electronics to drain and for the moisture to fully evaporate. You might also leave the door open during this time to help airflow.
Done, dried it with a towel and left it off at the cooker switch for 5 mins, then switched back on. It came up normally, no E011, no beeping. It also heated to 180C fine. Is that all it was?

Yes, that was almost certainly the cause. The E011 error combined with your description of moisture on the panel and the immediate recovery after drying and resetting confirms a temporary short circuit in the control electronics caused by the damp cloth.
